headline: Tanzania Strikes Natural Gas Gold After a Decade of Waiting
meta_description: Tanzania celebrates its first major natural gas find in over 10 years at Mnazi Bay, bringing 223 billion cubic feet of energy to fuel growth.
summary_short: Tanzania has announced a significant natural gas discovery in Mnazi Bay—the first in more than a decade—marking a major milestone for the nation's energy future.
body:
Tanzania has discovered 223 billion cubic feet of natural gas in the Mnazi Bay area, marking a watershed moment for the East African nation's energy independence. The find, jointly owned by state-owned Tanzania Petroleum Development Corporation and French firm Maurel & Prom, represents the country's first major discovery in over ten years. Energy Minister Juma Homera called it a "major milestone" for Tanzania's developing oil and gas sector, emphasizing that the new well—the Kasa-1X ST2—will boost domestic supplies and ensure the country has "reliable, clean and safe energy at affordable costs." Production is expected to begin early next month, arriving at a time when industrial growth is driving up demand across the nation.

The discovery matters not just for energy security but for everyday Tanzanian life. Natural gas already powers nearly 80 percent of the country's electricity generation. Beyond power plants, the fuel is reshaping transport: Dar es Salaam now hosts natural gas filling stations where residents are converting vehicles to run on compressed natural gas—a cheaper alternative to petrol that's becoming increasingly accessible to ordinary people.

This find builds on Tanzania's long history with natural gas. The country made its first discovery in 1974 on Songo Songo Island, followed by a second at Mnazi Bay in 1982. The real transformation came in 2004 when commercialisation began, spurring decades of exploration. The largest previous discovery came in 2016, when 2.7 trillion cubic feet were found. With existing reserves already standing at 57.54 trillion cubic feet, today's announcement signals that Tanzania's energy future—and its capacity to power growth—continues to expand.
quick_facts: 223 billion cubic feet of natural gas discovered at Mnazi Bay
First major find in Tanzania in more than 10 years
Production to start early next month at Kasa-1X ST2 well
Natural gas powers 80 percent of Tanzania's electricity
Jointly owned by Tanzania Petroleum Development Corporation and Maurel & Prom
